value.body: A quality engineer sets up the checks and processes that make sure manufactured parts and products meet standards. Automotive suppliers, engineering goods and electronics manufacturers hire them. A day involves inspecting parts, analysing defects, handling customer complaints, and maintaining quality documents and audits.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech / B.E. in Mechanical or Production

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers join as graduate engineer trainees or junior quality engineers through campus placement at manufacturers. A Six Sigma Green Belt or quality tools course can help with shortlisting.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Measurement and inspection using gauges and CMM
Preparing quality documents such as PPAP and FMEA

value.title: At a glance
items: Customer audits and complaint handling are a regular part of the job.
Common next roles: supplier quality engineer, quality manager, Six Sigma or process roles.
Automotive quality roles follow strict industry standards.
